lens: validity, reliability, fairness, and evaluation design

findings.observation: The implementation does not keep the release-blocking P0 set independent from the development and red-team banks. The same scenario documents are reused across suites, and TS-MEM-001 is simultaneously part of the P0 release suite and still labeled as a dev case.
findings.evidence: pasted-text-1.txt:49-58 requires P0, dev, held_out, and red_team to remain independent. evals/v2/suites/p0-release.v1.json:8-117 reuses scenario IDs that also remain in initial-coverage-36, and evals/v2/suites/initial-coverage-36.v1.json:207-214 still marks TS-MEM-001 as partition dev while it is included in p0-release.v1.json:73-80.
findings.user_impact: A builder can tune against a case that later appears to be an independent release gate, so a passing P0 result no longer means the release slice was protected from development-set contamination.
findings.recommendation: Make the release gate a disjoint frozen slice with no scenario overlap against dev, held_out, or red_team, or explicitly downgrade any claim of independent release evidence until the partition model is rebuilt.
findings.verification: A repository check fails whenever any scenarioId or contentDigest appears in more than one of the P0, dev, held_out, and red_team slices, and the repaired suite shows zero overlap before release runs are accepted.

findings.criterion: Atomic ground truth and adjudication validity
findings.observation: The review contract says human gold belongs to atomic criterion-plus-evidence decisions, but the runtime contracts only store adjudication once per scenario. That collapses partially reviewed and disputed criteria into one scenario-level label.
findings.evidence: pasted-text-1.txt:331-335 says human_gold binds to atomic criterion and evidence locator. packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:181-199 defines a single scenario-level adjudication field, packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:308-316 repeats that single field in suite registrations, and apps/eval-runner/src/opik/syncDataset.ts:19-31 exports only the same scenario-level adjudication value.
findings.user_impact: A scenario can appear fully human_gold even when only some criteria were adjudicated, which weakens calibration, held-out trust, and any claim that a specific atomic evaluator has independent gold supervision.
findings.recommendation: Store adjudication at the criterion level with explicit evidence locators and disagreement state, then derive any scenario-level summary from those atomic records instead of treating the whole scenario as uniformly gold.
findings.verification: One scenario with mixed criterion outcomes can be represented as partly human_gold and partly disputed, and dataset export preserves those atomic statuses without upgrading unresolved criteria.

findings.observation: The model-review rubric requires adjudication and repeat-stability evidence, but the calibration code can still mark a judge eligible for non-P0 informational use without measuring either of those requirements. The order-swap calculation also trusts orderPairId alone, so unrelated decisions can be counted as a stable pair.
findings.evidence: evals/v2/rubrics/model-soft-quality.v1.json:14-18 requires confusion_matrix, raw_agreement, false_pass, false_fail, abstention, adjudication, order_swap_stability, and repeat_stability. apps/eval-runner/src/calibration.ts:57-154 computes confusion matrix, raw agreement, false pass, false fail, abstention, and orderStability, and lines 103-115 can still set eligibleForNonP0InformationalUse to true. apps/eval-runner/src/calibration.ts:78-89 groups pairs only by orderPairId and does not verify that original and swapped records refer to the same scenarioId and criterionId.
findings.user_impact: The team can grant model-review eligibility on thinner evidence than the rubric promises, which makes informational quality labels look better calibrated than they really are and can bias experiment triage.
findings.recommendation: Extend the calibration artifact and eligibility rule to require adjudication rate, repeat-stability, and pair-integrity checks on scenarioId plus criterionId before any model judge is marked eligible.
findings.verification: A calibration summary remains ineligible until all required measures are present, and a malformed pair with one original and one swapped decision from different criteria is rejected instead of inflating stability.

findings.criterion: Construct validity of Scenario × Profile pairing
findings.observation: Scenario, Profile, and Attempt are physically separated, but there is no enforceable compatibility rule between a scenario and the profile used to run it. The CLI accepts arbitrary profile overrides, and execution validity only checks that the selected profile has a non-frozen declared system under test.
findings.evidence: pasted-text-1.txt:53 and pasted-text-1.txt:169-240 require a stable Scenario meaning across profiles. packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:181-199 gives scenarios no compatible-profile contract beyond advisory slices metadata, apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:166-169 accepts any --profile override, and apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:32-52 plus 75-96 validate only systemUnderTest shape and oracle leak boundaries rather than scenario-profile semantic compatibility.
findings.user_impact: An invalid experiment can still produce a formally versioned Attempt and Gate, which risks comparing runs that test different constructs while presenting them as if they were commensurate evaluation evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit compatible profile or mode declarations, or a scenario capability requirement matrix, and reject runs whose selected profile does not match the scenario's declared construct boundary.
findings.verification: Replaying an identity scenario against an unrelated search or effect-adapter profile is rejected before manifest creation, while approved scenario-profile combinations still run and remain reproducible.

strengths: The repository cleanly separates semantic scenarios from model input, initial state, and oracle fixtures, which is the right foundation for oracle independence and replayability.
The local gate is veto-first rather than average-first, and a P0 deterministic failure cannot be overwritten by softer quality signals.
Local manifest creation and local gate recording happen before optional Opik projection, so projection failure does not become silent truth loss.
The repository validate command and suite inventory prove that a real 36-case bank and a 12-case P0 bank now exist with versioned digests and typed profiles.
missing_evidence: No implementation evidence in the reviewed code shows the contamination controls promised in pasted-text-1.txt:333-335, especially semantic-near-duplicate scanning across dev, held_out, red_team, and P0 slices.

No frozen artifact in docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform demonstrates a real 60-decision model-judge calibration run; the proof bundle is an Opik smoke proof and explicitly excludes a model-quality improvement claim.
No criterion-level human-gold store or read path is visible in the reviewed contracts, so there is no independent artifact proving that disputed and confirmed criterion labels survive into reporting.
open_questions: Should P0 remain a separate disjoint release slice, or do you intend it to reuse cases from the development bank and therefore give up the independence claim in pasted-text-1.txt?
Where will criterion-level gold and disagreement records live so one scenario can carry mixed adjudication states without laundering unresolved criteria into human_gold?
